Class SwingGate

java.lang.Object
dev.swordai.core.rl.SwingGate
public final class SwingGate extends Object
No swing before the weapon is back. Whatever the network says, the attack key is not its to press until the weapon has recharged this far; it then decides whether to swing, as before.

A swing made early is never the better swing: it does a fraction of the damage, it cannot knock back or be critical (the game asks for more than nine tenths of the charge for either), and it starts the weapon over, so the proper hit that was a few ticks away is gone as well. In training the network had learned that from what an early swing cost it, and made one swing in ten early. But what it had really learned was a rhythm that held in the arena: the opponent flies off when it is hit and is back in reach about when the weapon is. Against a player on a server with 200 ms each way, the opponent is seen to be knocked back nine or ten ticks after the click and stands in reach, under the crosshair, the whole time the weapon recharges. There it swung again and again: six to seven swings in ten were early (0.13.2), nearly every hit was a weak one, and it lost to a beginner. A rule the game itself never bends is better kept than learned.

The line is drawn a tick later than the game needs. On a server the swings arrive a tick apart more or less than they were made, and a swing made on the first tick the client sees the weapon back can reach the server on a tick it does not: no knockback, no critical hit. Twelve ticks after the last swing (0.96 of a sword's 12.5) leaves that tick to spare, at the cost of one tick of rhythm.

    • EARLY_CHARGE

      public static final float EARLY_CHARGE
      The default for Config.swingMinCharge, since 18 October: eleven ticks after the last swing, 0.88 on its own screen, which the game makes 0.92 when the swing is made (it adds half a tick): more than the nine tenths it asks for knockback and a critical hit, and nine tenths of the damage. The user's words: a hit with the sword 90% back "is considered ok in game". A player who has found out that it swings the moment its sword is all the way back, and never before, can time his own hit to come down a tick before that; the tick is the network's to use or not. Swings a rule makes for it still wait for MIN_CHARGE.
      See Also:

  • Method Details

    • outOfReach

      public static boolean outOfReach(float[] vec)
      The opponent is plainly out of reach, or nowhere on the screen: a swing now hits nothing, starts the sword over, and hands the opponent a free hit in its cooldown. The user, 18 October, of 0.15.0: it "swing in air and gets MANY free hit" (14 of its 18 misses were from beyond 3 blocks, most of them in the air after being knocked back). The distance is read off the opponent's height on screen, as the network sees it; not with the opponent cut off by the screen's edge, since then it is close and its height says nothing.

    • keys

      public static int keys(int headMask, float charge, float minCharge)
      The keys the network has on this tick: headMask, less the attack key while the weapon is not back.
      Parameters:
      charge - how far the weapon has recharged, 0 to 1, as the fighter's own game counts it
      minCharge - the least charge a swing may be made with; zero or less leaves every swing to the network
